subject: Pricing follow-up: validating monthly spend band & procurement thresholds
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@atlasai.io>, Marco Jimenez <marco.j@atlasai.io>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing follow-up: validating monthly spend band & procurement thresholds

Hi Elena / Marco —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we discussed and a couple of concrete asks so we can prep a tailored pricing package and procurement path: 

Recap / request list:
- Estimated monthly token volume: you mentioned a pilot of 150M–300M tokens/month, with production north of 1B tokens/month if ML perf and latency look good. Please confirm which scenario we should model first.
- Target unit economics: you asked for a baseline cost to model against. Our starting proposal is $100 / 1M tokens for hosted tiers; committed dedicated reservations can drop that to ~$65–80 / 1M depending on term and burst guarantees.
- Monthly spend band to validate for procurement: is Atlas comfortable with an initial PO range of $5k–$25k / month for the pilot, with a procurement threshold at $25k/month that would trigger a longer-term committed agreement? If procurement requires a single-year commitment for >$25k/month, please confirm.
- Procurement contacts: sending to procurement@atlasai.io to surface any internal routing requirements (PO vs contract, SSO/KMS requirements).

Next steps we propose:
1) Atlas confirms which token scenario to price (pilot 150–300M vs scale 1B+).
2) We’ll send a clean, line-item pricing worksheet and SOW draft for legal/procurement to review (attached: RDW-pricing-model-v2.xlsx, SOW-draft-AtlasAI.pdf).
3) Internal alignment call (10–20m) with procurement if you want to review thresholds/discount tables.

If you prefer, I can model three pricing outcomes (pilot, mid-growth, scaled) and include the per-1M-token blended rate, expected monthly spend, and recommended reserved discount level.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@atlasai.io>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Jimenez <marco.j@atlasai.io>, Atlas AI Procurement <procurement@atlasai.io>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: validating monthly spend band & procurement thresholds

Thanks Laura — useful summary. Two clarifications from our side before we loop in procurement: 

1) Pilot target: please model the pilot at 250M tokens/month (average). We have 3 internal apps feeding traffic; combined baseline sits around that number.
2) For procurement: our internal procurement team has an approval threshold at $20k/month for SaaS spend without a full contracting cycle. Anything above $20k/month typically requires a one-year master services agreement and legal review.

Can you adjust the proposed procurement threshold to $20k/month instead of $25k? Also, please include an example blended rate that shows the break-even point between hosted usage vs a 12-month committed Dedicated plan (i.e., at what monthly token volume does dedication become cheaper).

Appreciate it — copying procurement to start the legal thread.

Elena
Head of Product | Atlas AI
elena@atlasai.io
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena@atlasai.io>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Pricing follow-up: validating monthly spend band & procurement thresholds

Looping in unit-econ details and a quick model. High level first, then numbers: 

- Baseline hosted: $100 / 1M tokens (no commitment).
- 3‑month reserved burst (short commit): effective $85–90 / 1M depending on sustained draw.
- 12‑month Dedicated (committed capacity): baseline $65 / 1M at 1B tokens/month, sliding up to $80 / 1M at 300M tokens/month.

Quick break-even math (approx):
- If you run 250M tokens/month: hosted @ $100 => $25K/month. A 12-month Dedicated priced at $75 / 1M => $18.75K/month (so Dedicated is ~25% cheaper at this volume with a 12-month commit).
- If you run 150M tokens/month: hosted => $15K/month; Dedicated @ $80 / 1M => $12K/month (savings smaller, procurement may prefer hosted initially to avoid contract).

Recommendation for Atlas pilot (250M/month):
- Show procurement two paths: (A) hosted monthly + short-term credits to keep initial spend under $20k (we can apply onboarding credits to net under procurement threshold); or (B) 12‑month Dedicated at an effective $75 / 1M with PO for the year (procurement favors predictability).

I attached the spreadsheet with the blended-rate table and sensitivity (RDW-pricing-model-v2.xlsx). Happy to run additional scenarios if procurement gives us the exact approval thresholds and preferred term length.

—
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
From: Atlas AI Procurement <procurement@atlasai.io>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena@atlasai.io>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: validating monthly spend band & procurement thresholds

Hi Laura / Aditya —

Procurement notes: 
- Our approval threshold is $20,000/month for recurring SaaS spend without a signed MSA. Anything above this amount requires a one-year MSA signed by legal + our finance team issue a PO.
- For pilot work where we want to avoid a full MSA, Atlas can accept a merchant agreement with an explicit cap and an initial 3-month term, provided the vendor accepts our standard Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and SOC2 evidence.
- Billing cadence: monthly invoicing is preferred; finance will waive net-30 only under a signed MSA.

Actions required from Redwood to move forward:
1) Confirm if onboarding credits can be applied to the first 2 months to keep billed spend <= $20k/month.
2) Confirm Redwood's acceptance of Atlas DPA (we attach a standard DPA to this thread separately).
3) Provide SOC2 report and a single point of contact for invoicing.

Procurement will schedule a short call if needed after the pricing worksheet is updated.

Regards,
Marco Jimenez
Procurement Manager | Atlas AI
procurement@atlasai.io
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Atlas AI Procurement <procurement@atlasai.io>, Elena Ruiz <elena@atlasai.io>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: validating monthly spend band & procurement thresholds

Thanks Marco — appreciate the clarity. Quick responses and next steps: 

1) Onboarding credits: yes, we can apply onboarding credits to reduce billed spend for months 1–2. Proposed structure: apply $7,500 credit in month 1 and $5,000 credit in month 2. This brings a 250M tokens/month pilot from $25k to ~$17.5k in month 1 and $20k in month 2 (depending on exact token consumption).
2) DPA / SOC2: Redwood accepts Atlas’s DPA pending a brief legal review. I will attach our SOC2 Type II report and point Sean Gallagher (cc'd) as the SOC2 contact for procurement.
3) Invoicing: Redwood can do monthly invoicing. Net-30 requires MSA; otherwise standard monthly billing preferred.

Next steps from Redwood: I’ll upload the updated pricing worksheet with the onboarding-credit rows and break-even chart, and share a 20-minute slot for a procurement alignment call later this week. If procurement is happy, we’ll prepare a short merchant agreement that includes the credit schedule and an optional 12-month committed appendix.

Attachments: RDW-pricing-model-v2.xlsx, SOW-draft-AtlasAI.pdf

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
